Is physical therapy covered under my Silver plan?

Yes, physical therapy is covered under your Silver Select plan. Coverage is limited to 30 visits per calendar year, and prior authorization is required beyond the initial evaluation. Your copay is $40 per visit after your deductible is met. Disclaimer: This is general plan information, not medical advice. Consult a licensed provider for medical decisions.

Your Silver Select plan has an individual deductible of $1,500 per calendar year and a family deductible of $3,000. Once you meet your deductible, the plan begins sharing costs for covered services. Under federal balance billing protections, you will be billed at the in-network rate for emergency services. After stabilization, continued care may require transfer to an in-network facility. You may also be balance-billed for charges above the plan's allowable amount. Disclaimer: This is general plan information, not medical advice. Consult a licensed provider for medical decisions.

How do I appeal a denied claim?

You have the right to appeal a denied claim. To start an appeal, contact member services within 180 days of receiving the denial notice. You can submit a written appeal with supporting medical documentation. An internal review will be completed within 30 days for non-urgent claims. You also have the right to an external review if your internal appeal is denied. Disclaimer: This is general plan information, not medical advice. Consult a licensed provider for medical decisions.

What is coinsurance and how does it work?

Coinsurance is your share of the cost of a covered service after you've paid your deductible. Under your Silver Select plan, after meeting your deductible, you pay 20% (coinsurance) for most in-network services, and the plan pays the remaining 80%. For example, a $500 procedure would cost you $100 in coinsurance. Disclaimer: This is general plan information, not medical advice. Consult a licensed provider for medical decisions.

What is the difference between a copay and a deductible?

A deductible is the amount you pay out of pocket before your plan begins sharing costs — your Silver Select deductible is $1,500. A copay is a fixed amount you pay for a specific service (like $50 for a specialist visit) regardless of whether you've met your deductible. Some services, like preventive care, don't require you to meet the deductible first. Disclaimer: This is general plan information, not medical advice. Outside of open enrollment, you can add a dependent within 30 days of a qualifying life event such as the birth or adoption of a child, marriage, or a dependent losing other coverage.
